name: SYNERGY
question: Does solifenacin plus mirabegron improve urinary incontinence and frequency more than either drug alone in adults with wet overactive bladder?

design.population: Adults with wet overactive bladder for at least 3 months, at least 8 daily micturitions, at least 1 daily urgency episode, and at least 3 incontinence episodes in a 7-day diary after placebo run-in.
design.description: Multinational, double-blind, six-arm superiority randomized trial
design.locator: Herschorn 2017, Patients and methods; Results, patient disposition; Table 1

verdictNote: The first co-primary comparison missed, stopping the multiplicity-controlled testing sequence.
takeaway: Over 12 weeks, solifenacin 5 mg plus mirabegron 50 mg reduced daily incontinence more than solifenacin 5 mg alone but did not meet prespecified superiority over mirabegron 50 mg; subsequent frequency testing was blocked. A lower-dose combination and placebo were also studied.

reports.label: Primary 12-week report
reports.citation: Herschorn S, Chapple CR, Abrams P, et al. "Efficacy and safety of combinations of mirabegron and solifenacin compared with monotherapy and placebo in patients with overactive bladder (SYNERGY study)." *BJU Int.* 2017;120(4):562-575. doi:10.1111/bju.13882
reports.followUp: 12 weeks of double-blind treatment; 2-week placebo run-out

results.measure: Adjusted mean difference in change from baseline to week 12: solifenacin 5 mg plus mirabegron 50 mg versus solifenacin 5 mg
results.note: Rank ANCOVA P value and parametric confidence interval use different methods; the confidence interval crosses zero.

results.measure: Adjusted mean difference in change from baseline to week 12: solifenacin 5 mg plus mirabegron 50 mg versus mirabegron 50 mg
results.note: First co-primary testing step required superiority to both monotherapies; primary objective was not met.

results.measure: Placebo-adjusted mean difference in change from baseline to week 12
results.note: Combination-versus-monotherapy frequency comparisons had nominal P values only after the incontinence testing sequence stopped.

results.endpoint: Zero urinary incontinence episodes at end of treatment
results.measure: Responders in the last 3 diary days
results.note: Exploratory pairwise responder comparisons were outside the stopped confirmatory sequence.

harms.label: Urinary retention, sponsor-defined terms
harms.locator: Table 4, safety analysis set; footnote on preferred and lower-level terms
harms.note: Four retention events required catheterization: two in each combination group.

delivery.label: Treatment schedule
delivery.value: Four-week single-blind placebo run-in, 12 weeks of once-daily double-blind therapy, then 2-week placebo run-out.

delivery.label: Trial disposition
delivery.value: 3,527 randomized; 3,494 received double-blind treatment; 3,398 in the safety set and 3,308 in the full analysis set; 96 treated patients from one site excluded from both analysis sets for protocol noncompliance.

delivery.label: Enrollment setting
delivery.locator: Results, Patient demographics and baseline characteristics

delivery.label: Baseline symptom and treatment history
delivery.value: In the 3,398-person safety set, 2,223 (65.4%) had urgency incontinence only and 1,577 (46.4%) had used prior OAB medication.

reports.label: Patient-reported outcomes
reports.citation: Robinson D, Kelleher C, Staskin D, et al. "Patient-reported outcomes from SYNERGY, a randomized, double-blind, multicenter study evaluating combinations of mirabegron and solifenacin compared with monotherapy and placebo in OAB patients." *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2018;37(1):394-406. doi:10.1002/nau.23315

results.endpoint: OAB-q symptom bother and health-related quality of life
results.note: Both combination groups improved symptom bother versus monotherapies (nominal P<0.001) and HRQOL total scores (P≤0.002); abstract gives no absolute score changes.

reports.label: Cardiovascular safety
reports.citation: White WB, Chapple C, Gratzke C, et al. "Cardiovascular Safety of the β3-Adrenoceptor Agonist Mirabegron and the Antimuscarinic Agent Solifenacin in the SYNERGY Trial." *J Clin Pharmacol.* 2018;58(8):1084-1091. doi:10.1002/jcph.1107

harms.label: Adjudicated major cardiovascular events
harms.note: Mean heart rate increased by approximately 1 beat/min in mirabegron groups; no clinically meaningful between-group QTcF differences were reported.

relations.note: Same solifenacin-plus-mirabegron program; BESIDE enrolled patients still incontinent after four weeks of solifenacin 5 mg.
